name: Pearl Green
lede: Pearl Green is a dark, slightly yellowish green from the German RAL paint standard, and it is a near-exact computed match for the archive's Spruce Green.

sections.title: A pearl that is actually green
sections.body:
Our library catalogues this color as RAL 6035, from the RAL industrial color standard first published in Germany in 1927 [1]. It shares the small "Pearl" naming family with [[heather-grey|Pearl Blackberry]] and [[pearl-gentian|Pearl Gentian]], a purple and a teal: the three names have nothing in common but a borrowed gem-word, since a real [[gem:pearl|pearl]] carries almost no color at all [1]. The ISCC-NBS system calls its block "dark yellowish green"; in Munsell it reads 0.9G 3.1/6.0 [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[spruce-green|Spruce green]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 0.0 — the two names resolve to the same computed swatch [1]. [[spruce|Spruce]] itself sits close too, at 4.3 units, making this a crowded corner of dark conifer greens [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pearl Green appears in 45 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.19 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 23 of them, rarer than 60 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 5 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.4 times the expected rate for that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a shadow, in 39 percent of the 23 paintings where it carries real area [2].

The earliest match is dated 1790, in a portrait by Charles Peale Polk — 137 years before RAL's 1927 record of the name, as photographed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The gap is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof that this exact paint existed that early [2].
